title: Loomings — Action Spine
adaptation_principle: Prioritize Ishmael’s concrete decisions and acceptances over Melville’s broad meditations. Stage reflections with the narrator in simple, present physical actions on shore, compressing rhetorical catalogs into captions. Do not visualize hypotheticals or metaphors; carry them in first-person captions. Use the fewest frames that preserve the chapter’s action turns.
action_oriented_synopsis: Feeling grim and restless, I decide to go to sea to set myself right. I choose to ship before the mast rather than travel as a passenger or command as an officer, and I make my peace with the humble knocks of the life. I prefer being paid and the wholesome air. Drawn—almost fated—toward a whaling voyage, my curiosity about the great whale and remote seas opens the gates to the wonder-world, and I welcome the voyage.
caption_spine: Call me Ishmael—when I grow grim, I take to the ship to see the watery part of the world.
I never go as a passenger or officer; when I go to sea, I go as a simple sailor, right before the mast.
However they may order and thump me about, I count it the universal thump and rub my shoulder-blades, and am content.
I go as a sailor because they pay me, and for the wholesome exercise and pure air of the forecastle.
But now I took it into my head to go on a whaling voyage, as if some invisible police officer of the Fates had me in tow.
The great whale and the wild distant seas tormented my curiosity, so the flood-gates of the wonder-world swung open to me.

visual_safety_notes: Do not depict hypothetical scenes (e.g., a captain ordering Ishmael to sweep) as actual events; keep such ideas in captions while staging neutral dockside actions.
Avoid visualizing metaphors or inner images (e.g., the grand hooded phantom, processions of whales); keep the horizon empty of such figures.
Use only generic ships and docks with no readable names, signs, or labels; include the phrase ‘No readable text’ in prompts.
Limit people on screen to Ishmael and anonymous background silhouettes; do not introduce named historical figures or specific captains.
Keep animals and extra objects minimal and generic; do not add creatures not mentioned in the scene.
Maintain period-appropriate but unbranded clothing and props to prevent unintended text or specific identifications.
